title: Box Office Domestic 7 Billion
report:
A year with a global total of $3B+ on 12 movies (and an additional 1.1 from reissues), the B.O. is -9% behind where we were in2019. 

A summer of superhero titles at the forefront, including Warners Bros’ The Flash ($629.4M), which did not quite match DC’s last year’s results due to a later release date and also underperforming with only a 34% retention from the prior film), Marvel Studios’ Spider-Verse getting back on track with Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania (a -35% decline from last year’s total of $1.03B, which had already been the lowest since the first one). The title is projected to do well at Thanksgiving but will fall -32% behind Homecoming ($742M), a -44% drop from the second in the franchise. Disney+/Pixar’s Lightyear (a +28% improvement from last year’s $243.7M, which was also 6% higher than its first film) rounds out the Top 10.

While Disney has two movies on this list, Sony and Universal each have three titles at home to one, with Illumination taking a break between films.

title: Best New Soulslikes Ranked
report:
This action-RPG is an excellent game, with a lot of attention paid to sound design. Its colorful art style and anime-influenced cutscenes make for some impressive visual variety in gameplay. If you’re new to Soulslikes, Another Crab's Treasure is one of the best games of last year to get started with. But this hidden gem also has some clever mechanics that are worth keeping an eye on as a great series develops.
7 Death's Door (2023)
Where to play: PC
Death’s Door is a little-known indie Soulslike developed by a team led by a 1-person development team. It is very much like other Souls games, but its own identity, setting, and mysterious storytelling make it worth playing. There is also some really interesting mechanics to explore, such as the Memory system.
6 Uncharted (2007)
Where to play: PlayStation 3, Xbox 360
The original Uncharted has many elements of a third-person shooter, action-RPG, and open-world game rolled into one with a compelling narrative that makes for an great first experience in this series. Its linear design is refreshing, and Drakes’s charm is undeniable.
5 The Last Oric (2008)
Where to play: PlayStation 3
The second Uncharted title expands on the first, while staying true to its action-RPG formula with a mix of set pieces and exploration. It also has one of the best villains in gaming history, in our opinion, with Ratchet’s wise-cracking humor.
4 Salt and Sanctuary (2020)
Where to play: PC
Salt and Sanctuary is an underrated Soulslike that has some really cool systems, such as its magic system that allows players build their own spells. It also has a good atmosphere and story, which will be continued in this year’s Elden Ring.
3 Nioh: Complete Edition (2016)
Where to play: PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch, Windows, Xbox One
Nioh: Complete Edition is an enhanced version of the original action-RPG with a dark, gothic setting. Its depth and complexity make it still worth playing today, especially for the fans who enjoy a challenge.
2 The Surge (2020)
Where to play: PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch, Windows, Xbox One
The Surge is one of the best games that combines elements from different genres in an action-RPG with soulslike gameplay. Its world and combat system make it so enjoyable to play, while its atmosphere and sound design set it apart.
1 Sekiro Kishi (2020)
Where to play: PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch, Windows, Xbox One
Sekiro Kishi is a hidden gem that brings Japanese folklore into the Soulsborne genre. Its atmospheric setting and narrative make it worth playing.

Notes:

*Games are listed in order of their release year and then alphabetical by title.
* All games featured have a metacritic score above 80% on PC Gamerankings to qualify for this list.
* The ranking is subjective, but there are many other great Soulslikes that didn’t make the cut-off, so apologies if your favorite isn’t here.
